1. Project Abstract & Executive Summary

Post-harvest produce spoilage accounts for significant economic losses in global agriculture and supply-chain logistics. Manual grading is labor-intensive, subjective, and prone to human inspection fatigue, while existing computer vision prototypes often rely on single brittle architectures that lack explainability and industrial persistence.

This project presents FreshHarvest AI, an end-to-end, multi-model deep learning system designed for automated fruit variety recognition and freshness quality assessment. The system implements, evaluates, and benchmarks three state-of-the-art Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architectures: EfficientNet-B0, ResNet-50, and MobileNet-V2. To solve the opacity of deep neural networks, Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) is integrated to generate explainable visual heatmaps pinpointing localized decay and surface lesions. An automated consensus voting mechanism synthesizes predictions across all three architectures to guarantee high reliability, while a robust SQLite database audit trail, batch ZIP processing engine, and full Flask web dashboard provide enterprise-ready deployment.

2. Project Objectives & Scope
  • Produce Classification: Joint Fruit Variety Recognition and Freshness Classification across 14 balanced classes (Apple, Banana, Lemon, Mango, Orange, Strawberry, Tomato).
  • Tri-Model Comparative Benchmarking: Implement, fine-tune, and benchmark EfficientNet-B0, ResNet-50, and MobileNet-V2 on standardized agricultural datasets.
  • Explainable AI (Grad-CAM): Produce visual convolutional activation heatmaps to interpret network decisions for agricultural inspectors.
  • Consensus Decision Engine: Implement a multi-model voting engine calculating confidence agreement ratios (3/3 Unanimous vs. 2/3 Majority).
  • Industrial Software Portal: Provide multi-image/ZIP batch inspection with CSV export, historical SQLite persistence, and Chart.js analytics.
3. Literature Review & Base Repository Comparison

This project builds upon and significantly improves the baseline architecture established in erickyegon/FreshHarvest (Erick Kiprotich Yegon, 2024). The table below details the engineering advancements introduced in FreshHarvest AI:

Project Dimension Base Reference (erickyegon/FreshHarvest) FreshHarvest AI (This Work)
Model Architectures 1 single model active at a time Tri-Model concurrent pipeline (EfficientNet-B0, ResNet-50, MobileNet-V2)
Classification Scope Binary Fresh vs. Spoiled only Joint recognition: 7 fruit varieties × 2 conditions = 14 unified classes
Explainable AI None (Black-box inference) Full Grad-CAM activation heatmaps with Jet colormap alpha blending
Consensus Decision Single model decision only Tri-model confidence voting & agreement ratio ensemble
Batch Screening Single image upload only Industrial multi-image & ZIP archive batch inspection with CSV export
Database Persistence Ephemeral (No persistence) SQLite database (database.db) with predictions, metrics, and audit tables
Web Dashboard Basic inline HTML Responsive Bootstrap 5 UI, Chart.js analytics, and REST API endpoints

9. Conclusion & Project Defense Checklist

The FreshHarvest AI project successfully designed, implemented, and benchmarked an enterprise-ready fruit freshness and quality assessment system. By benchmarking EfficientNet-B0, ResNet-50, and MobileNet-V2 across 14 balanced produce classes, the system demonstrated high classification accuracy (up to 94.12%), balanced parameter efficiency, and sub-20ms inference latency.
